text: SAFETY MEN TO STAY ON DUTY.

label: text
text: "I can say" plainly that the Miners Federation is "unable in any part of Britain to withdraw real safety men," declared. Mr. Shirkie, Secretary of the National Federation of Colliery Enginemen, Boilernen, and Mechanics in an interview with Reuter.

label: text
text: He added: "We don't take their resolution seriously" because practically all of the safetymen were controlled by his Federation which was not going to withdraw them. —Reuter.

label: text
text: The Executive Council of the National Federation of Colliery Enginemen, Boilermen and Mechanics, which controls practically all the safetymen, has decided not to withdraw the safetymen from the confirries.

label: text
text: How the coal shortage, in consequence of the British strike, is hampering the Continental manufacturers is illustrated by Gothenburg recording the imminence of a fuel famine.

text:

label: text
text: As it is now impossible to secure coal for November delivery prices for later delivery are bounding daily.

label: text
text: A contract of 5,000 tons has been lodged in America at 54/- a ton. Difficulties are accentuated by the freight rates having been recently doubled.—Reuter.

The Leicestershire Miners' Council has decided to call off the strike

label: text
text: Nearly 60 per cent. of the I.cestershire miners had already resumed.—Reuter.

label: text
text: It will not be known until next Thursday if the miners' district Lodges approve of the latest suggestion of the Delegate Conference to withdraw the safety men from the pits.

label: text
text: The proposal is widely criticised as a "policy of despair," and, even if adopted, it is likely to be without effect.

label: text
text: The great majority of safety men are not affiliated to the Miners' Unions, and there is no possibility whatever that they will cease the work of keeping the pits in order, on which they have been engaged throughout the dispute.

label: text
text: Even if the safety workers who are in the Miners' Unions responded to the call, there would be little difficulty in carrying on the work that they have been doing.—British Wireless Service.

text: “In view of the violation of party discipline by the most prominent members of the Opposition,” the Political Bureau of the Communist party has resolved to submit to the next plenary meeting of the committee of the Central Controlling Commission the question of imposing due party penalties on Trotsky, Zinovieff and Piatakoff.—Reuter.

label: text
text: An earlier message from Riguestated that the Moscow Committee of the Communist Party has requested the Central Committee to remonstrate with a number of leaders of the Opposition who are, allegedly responsible for many secret meetings and the distribution of much illegal literature. text: LOWEST FOR FIVE YEARS IN NEW YORK.

label: text
text: Cotton has dropped 82 points today—the lowest point for five years—following publication of the Government Estimates. Half of the loss was later recovered on heavy domestic selling. The foreign mill buying market closed at 42 to 50 points lower on the day. It is believed that a crop of seventeen million bales is certain with good weather.—Reuter.

label: text
text: President Coolidge has appointed a special committee of Government officials to investigate cotton market conditions and to recommend measures to relieve the situation arising from the slump in prices.—Router's American Service

Four Europeans and 100+ natives are entombed in the Durban Navigation Colliery at Darthauser as the result of an explosion in the shaft.
Eleven dead natives have so far been brought up by the rescuers, who are now searching the deeper levels.—Reuter.

RETIRES FROM AMBASSADOR
POST IN BERLIN.

label: text
text: A large crowd had gathered outside the palace in the Wilhelmstrasse, and Berlin correspondents state that the Ambassador's departure has provoked a remarkable display of regret on the part of all classes of Germans.

label: text
text: Addressing the President, the Ambassador reviewed the events during the six years of his mission. He mentioned the stabilisation of Germany's currency, after a crisis unparalleled in history, of Germany's passage through financial chaos to financial equilibrium, and the reorganisation of her industry and commerce upon a basis auguring well for the future material prosperity.

label: text
text: He added, "In the sphere of politics the transformation has been no less remarkable, and I leave Germany at peace with her neighbours, her security assured by the Treaty of Locarno, and her place among the nations at Geneva established by universal consent."

label: text
text: The President, in replying, said that the policy of permanent European peace had made an important step forward, and in that evolution Lord D'Abernon had taken a paramount share which would not be forgotten.

label: text
text: The Ambassador was presented by the Government of the Reich with a magnificent antique silver centrepiece.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Though Chang Tso-lin studiously refrains from seizing control of the Cabinet, and lets the powerless Wu Pei-fu nominees hang on to their jobs; he is gradually making water-tight his actual control of Peking and the surrounding territory.

label: text
text: When the commandant of the Peking Garrison, a Wu Pei-fu man, left the city last week, Chang Tso-lin's young son stepped in, assumed control of the garrison, and incorporated the garrison into the Feng-tien armies, announcing at the same time that General Wang had been superseded as a commander by General Yu Chen.

label: text
text: The Cabinet has decided to hang on for a time. Wu Pei-fu has wired urging the members not to desert, and Chang Tao-lin has told the members he does not want to displace them.

label: text
text: There has, however, been a re-shuffling of portfolios, in secret conferences. Dr. Wellington Koo, who has been Finance Minister, has transferred to the post of Foreign Minister. He will also henceforth be Acting Premier

label: text
text: The former Premier, Admiral Tu Hsei-kual, remains in the Cabinet as Minister of the Navy, and Mr. Pan Fu will probably succeed Mr. Koo as Minister of Finance. Admiral Tsai Ting-kan, ill in a French Hospital in the Legation Quarter, persists in resigning, and may leave the Cabinet.

label: text
text: On only one point has the new Cabinet (which is really the old re-arranged) announced, a policy. That policy is that the assets of the Defunct Russo-Asiatic Bank shall not be removed from China, and that the Chinese Government will oversee the entire liquidation proceedings.

label: text
text: The Government owns nearly 5,000,000 taels worth of stock in the bank, besides being a large creditor owing to the fact that a portion of the Customs and Salt Gabelle revenues were deposited with the institution.

label: text
text: composed entirely of Chinese bankers, is petitioning the Government to force the depositing of all Customs and Salt Gabells funds in Chinese banks.
